lessons.title: Stories Across Mediums
graderIssues: Word echo: "details" and "Match" recur across multiple slides — vary the wording so the teach word != example word.
Some highlightWord targets (e.g. details, exact) are not present in any on-screen displayText/displayParts — every highlightWord MUST appear in a visible on-screen anchor on that slide.

Keep the strong teach->example->fork spine; this is polish only. Standard RL.4.7 = how a visual/oral presentation reflects SPECIFIC text descriptions; keep modeling a specific text moment -> its visual realization.

steps.ttsScript: A story can be read as words, or watched as a movie.
Today we match a story's exact words to what we see on screen.
Authors give us exact details, like a green cloak with a silver clasp.
A good movie shows those very details on screen, not just any cloak.
Let's try one. Here is a line from a story.
The old lighthouse glowed red as waves crashed against the rocks.
steps.displayText: Lighthouse glowed red, waves crashed on rocks.

steps.ttsScript: Which detail must the movie show? A red glowing light!
And one more? Waves crashing on the rocks!
Here is a handy trick to remember.
Point to a detail in the words, then find that exact thing on screen.

currentSlides.heading: Your Turn!
currentSlides.spokenQ: Your turn, director! Here is a sentence: The knight raised a golden shield as the dragon breathed orange fire. To match these exact words, what must the movie show on screen?

interactive.hint: Look for the exact details in the sentence, then picture them on screen.
choices: A golden shield and orange fire
A castle on a tall hill
interactive.correct: A golden shield and orange fire
interactive.correctScript: Yes! A golden shield and orange fire. You matched the exact words to the screen!
interactive.wrongScript: Not quite. Look back at the exact details in the sentence. What could a camera actually show? Try again!

steps.ttsScript: Your turn! Let's match more story words to the screen.

lessons.title: Reading Big Stories
graderIssues: MISSING practice-intro slide entirely — the fork jumps straight to MCQs. ADD a practice-intro slide ("Your turn!" + a couple pills) after the interactive fork.

The Your Turn fork is a near-carbon-copy of the example (both: a scared kid at a daunting place inferring feeling from a physical tell). Make the fork a genuinely FRESH scenario/skill application, not the same frame.
Distractors "Bored"/"Sleepy" are weak giveaways. Use plausible same-emotion-category distractors (e.g. Excited, Confident, Nervous) so the kid must actually reason.
Word repeats across slides: clues / feels recur in multiple slides — vary the vocabulary.

steps.ttsScript: When a story gets longer, we read closely to understand it.
We watch the characters, the problem, and the clues.
Good readers ask who the story is about.
Then they ask what that person wants.
Watch for clues
that show how a hero feels
and what they do next.
Let's try one together. Here's part of a longer story.
Maya stared at the dark cave. Her hands shook, but she wanted to find her lost dog.
steps.displayText: Maya stared at the dark cave. Her hands shook, but she wanted to find her lost dog.

steps.ttsScript: How does Maya feel? Scared. Her shaking hands are the clue.
What does Maya want? To find her dog. That is why she keeps going.
Scared, but brave! You read the clues and understood Maya.
Here is a helpful trick.
Make a movie in your mind as you read each scene!
steps.displayText: Make a movie in your mind

steps.ttsScript: The clues become easy to see!

currentSlides.heading: Your Turn!
currentSlides.spokenQ: Your turn, detective! Here's a new story. Theo gripped the rope and looked up at the tall, steep cliff. He swallowed hard, but he wanted to reach the top first. How does Theo most likely feel as he looks up at the cliff?

interactive.hint: He swallowed hard before such a tall, steep climb. What clue does that give?
interactive.correctScript: Yes! Nervous! Swallowing hard before a steep climb was your clue!
interactive.wrongScript: So close! Look at the clue, he swallowed hard before a tall, steep cliff. Try again!
